engine: The first PHOTOGRAPHIC-map medium in the location family. A pre-baked STATIC mosaic of raster map tiles (satellite-style imagery of the real coordinates) laid out as a grid of plain tiles — NO canvas, NO live tile server, NO Leaflet/Mapbox, NO pan engine at runtime (stays no-WebGL, no second scroll owner). On reveal all tiles FORCE-DECODE (img.decode()) up front, THEN fade + scale in (scaleFrom -> 1) with a small per-tile diagonal stagger; then real POI dots DROP onto their real positions. The DECODE-GUARD is the whole point: an undecoded paints a black flicker, so we never reveal a tile that has not decoded.

measured_teardown.move: build a grid of .rtr-tile cells (one plain each, decoding=async) + .rtr-dot dots positioned by real x,y. decodeAll() forces img.decode() on EVERY tile before anything paints (cells start opacity:0 so hidden imgs decode without flicker). reveal() then transitions each cell opacity 0->1 + each img transform scale(scaleFrom)->scale(1), staggered by diagonal order (row+col)*stagger; once tiles are mostly in, dots drop (opacity 0->1, scale .4->1, translateY 10px->0) one after another. set(p 0..1) is a PURE reversible map of the same look across a scrub (tiles finish by p~0.62, dots land by p=1). will-change armed for the one-shot, cleared after.
measured_teardown.cited: NEW MEDIUM ROOT: all 12 existing location atoms are hand-drawn SVG or vector-baked OSM line-art; this is the first raster/photographic map. Production swaps the placeholder mosaic (a sliced render) for real baked satellite tiles of the OSM coordinates.

tiles.what: array of { src, col, row } — the pre-baked tile images and their grid position (0-based col/row). Lab = one render sliced into a CSS grid; production = real baked satellite tiles.

pois.what: array of { x, y, label } — real POI dots in 0..100 (% of the mosaic box). Use REAL OSM coordinates, never invented.

stagger.what: per-tile reveal delay along the diagonal sweep (row+col order). Smaller = tighter wave.

scaleFrom.what: image scale at the start of the reveal; eases to 1 (a gentle settle-in, not a zoom).

ease.what: reveal ease token: air | out | soft | none (or a raw cubic-bezier string).

auto.what: reveal once on scroll-into-view (ScrollTrigger 'top 78%', or rAF if no ScrollTrigger). false = manual: decode up front, you call reveal()/set() yourself.

entry: RasterTileReveal.create(target, opts) -> { reveal(), set(p), trigger, decodeAll(), refresh(), destroy }. target = .rtr-stage (the .rtr-mosaic + tiles + dots are injected). set(p 0..1) is a PURE reversible scrub of the whole timeline (staggered tiles then POI dots).
law: transform (scale/translateY) + opacity + filter only — NO width/height/top/left, NO mix-blend, NO backdrop, NO WebGL, NO canvas (plain tiles only), NO video scrub. GPU. DECODE-GUARD: every tile is force-decoded (img.decode()) before reveal/swap so an undecoded tile never paints a black flicker; cells start opacity:0 (hidden imgs still decode via the up-front decodeAll). will-change cleared after the one-shot. reduced-motion -> static (all tiles + dots shown, no motion). owns_pin false / owns_scroll false (the mosaic is frozen — only the reveal moves; no runtime pan/zoom engine).
gate_mode: scroll-into-view one-shot (auto:true) OR pure set(p) scrub (auto:false). Verify: ALL tiles decode before any paint (no black flicker — DevTools throttle network, no black cells); tiles fade + settle in with a diagonal stagger; real POI dots drop on their real positions; set(p) is reversible (p=0 hidden, p=1 fully shown). Distinct from every other location atom: this is a REAL raster map, not SVG/vector line-art.
proven: lab: the placeholder mosaic = renders/aerial.webp (1920x2560 QUADRO aerial) sliced into a 3x4 CSS grid of tiles via object-position, with 6 REAL Агрономічне POI dots (Траш!, Аврора, Грош Експрес, Нова Пошта, Подорожник, Школа·садок) projected onto the mosaic. Mechanic proven: decodeAll() resolves before reveal; tiles stagger in along the diagonal; dots drop after. window.__LAB_OK__ true, zero console errors. Production swaps in real baked satellite tiles of the OSM coordinates (note in RECIPE).
